DC-2025-B260167.title: Personal Medical Record Fee Exemption Amendment Act of 2025

actions.text: Public Hearing on B26-0167
Notice of Public Hearing filed in the Office of Secretary by Health
Referred to Committee on Health
Notice of Intent to Act on B26-0167 Published in the District of Columbia Register
B26-0167 Introduced by Chairman Mendelson at Office of the Secretary

documents.label: Notice of Public Hearing filed in the Office of Secretary by Health

DC-2025-B260167.aiSummary: The measure would stop health care entities in D.C. from charging fees for copies of personal medical records when they are needed for Social Security claims or appeals, or for other federal or District needs-based benefits or programs. It would apply when the records are requested by the patient, the patient’s representative, a nonprofit legal services worker, or the patient’s lawyer. It would take effect after mayoral approval, a 30-day congressional review period, and publication in the D.C. Register.

DC-2025-B260725.aiSummary: The measure would make the District of Columbia Department of Health set up a digital system for schools and health care providers to send student health and dental health forms. It would also stop providers from charging parents or guardians for those certificates. The bill would create a tiered fee plan for health professional licenses and registrations based on how much schooling the job needs.

documents.label: Notice of Public Hearing filed in the Office of Secretary by Judiciary and Publ…

DC-2025-B260549.aiSummary: The bill would limit District help with federal immigration enforcement unless there is a judicial warrant or court order. It would bar District staff from giving transport to federal agents for immigration enforcement, doing civil immigration patrols or surveillance, and joining immigration enforcement at places like schools, hospitals, shelters, libraries, and some other service sites unless there are exigent circumstances. It would also require District employees to be trained on these rules.

DC-2025-B260428.aiSummary: The bill would update District rules on jobs for minors. It would ban work for children under 14, set hour limits for 14- to 17-year-olds, and require employers to post the rules and keep age and time records. It would give the Department of Employment Services the job of issuing youth work permits, checking workplaces, and enforcing the law, and it would let the Attorney General bring court cases over violations.

DC-2025-B260093.aiSummary: The measure would ban the sale or fee-based installation of solely battery-powered smoke detectors that are not tamper-resistant in the District starting July 1, 2025. It would also let people file a written complaint with the Mayor about a violation, even if an inspector did not see it happen. A violation could lead to a civil fine of up to $500, plus penalties and fees.
